# Chapter 3: Requirements Analysis

## Overview

This chapter presents the requirements analysis for the **Machine Learning-Based System for Cardiopulmonary Sound Separation**. Requirements are gathered through literature and document review, existing system observation or benchmarking, supervisor consultation, and a structured questionnaire. The questionnaire is a required fact-finding method for collecting practical feedback on current challenges, preferred prototype features, interface design, result presentation, and evaluation needs.

The Google Form responses have not yet been collected. Therefore, this chapter presents the questionnaire design and analysis template only. The response findings and chart placeholders will be replaced after real Google Form responses are exported and analyzed. The chapter then defines preliminary functional, non-functional, and user requirements based on the project scope, literature review, supervisor consultation, and planned questionnaire analysis.

## Questionnaire

The questionnaire is used as a required fact-finding technique to validate user needs for the proposed prototype. It focuses on practical requirements rather than theoretical opinions. The questions are designed to identify the target users, understand their experience with audio or biomedical signal processing, identify problems in cardiopulmonary audio separation, and collect preferences for system features, interface design, output presentation, and evaluation metrics.

The full questionnaire contains 24 questions and is intended for inclusion in Appendix H. Chapter 3 analyzes only 10 main requirement-focused items to avoid repeating every questionnaire item in the report body. The full questionnaire supports traceability between the Google Form questions and the resulting system requirements.

### Questionnaire Design

The purpose of the questionnaire is to support Chapter 3 Requirements Analysis by collecting practical user requirements for the proposed cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype. The target respondents include Software Engineering or Computer Science students, AI or Machine Learning students, Biomedical Engineering or health-related students, researchers or students interested in biomedical audio or signal processing, and supervisors or evaluators where appropriate.

The questionnaire will be distributed using Google Forms. The estimated completion time is 3-5 minutes. The questionnaire introduction will state that the responses are collected for academic purposes, that there are no right or wrong answers, and that responses will remain confidential. The question types include multiple choice, checkbox, Likert-style scale, and paragraph response items. Response analysis is pending and will be completed only after real Google Form responses are collected.

Table @tbl-questionnaire-structure summarizes the questionnaire structure.

| Section | Purpose | Example question focus | Question type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Section A: Respondent Background | Identify respondent profile and relevant experience. | Age group, study area, signal processing familiarity, biomedical audio experience. | Multiple choice |
| Section B: Current Challenges in Cardiopulmonary Audio Processing | Identify problems users associate with cardiopulmonary audio processing. | Separation difficulty, noise, source overlap, recording quality, lack of tools. | Multiple choice, checkboxes, Likert-style scale |
| Section C: System Feature Preferences | Prioritize prototype features. | Upload, preprocessing, separation, preview, download, history, evaluation results. | Multiple choice, Likert-style scale |
| Section D: Interface and Output Preferences | Guide interface design and result presentation. | Audio player, waveform, spectrogram, metrics, interface simplicity, error messages. | Multiple choice, Likert-style scale |
| Section E: Evaluation and Improvement | Identify evaluation needs and improvement ideas. | Metrics, processing information, willingness to use the prototype, improvement suggestions. | Multiple choice, Likert-style scale, paragraph response |

### Respondent Background and Experience

Section A collected respondent background information, including respondent category, familiarity with audio or signal processing, biomedical audio experience, and audio-related task experience. These responses are used to confirm whether the questionnaire reached users who are relevant to the proposed cardiopulmonary sound separation system. Since this section is used mainly to describe the respondent profile, it is summarized in text instead of being presented as separate figures.

After Google Form responses are collected, this section will summarize the number of respondents, their academic or professional background, and their level of familiarity with audio processing, signal processing, biomedical audio, or machine learning. This respondent profile will help support the validity of the requirements analysis.

### Question 1: Difficulty of Separating Heart and Lung Sounds

This question measures how difficult respondents perceive the task of separating heart and lung sounds from a mixed cardiopulmonary recording. The purpose is to determine whether the project addresses a problem that users recognize as technically challenging.

![Perceived difficulty of separating heart and lung sounds](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q1_separation_difficulty_placeholder.png){#fig-q1-separation-difficulty}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will report whether respondents consider the task easy, neutral, difficult, or very difficult.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support the need for a machine learning-based separation function that processes mixed cardiopulmonary audio and generates separate heart and lung sound outputs.

### Question 2: Problems Affecting Cardiopulmonary Sound Processing

This question identifies the main problems that users believe affect cardiopulmonary sound processing. It focuses on practical issues such as background noise, overlap between heart and lung sounds, low recording quality, and lack of simple software tools.

![Problems affecting cardiopulmonary sound processing](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q2_processing_challenges_placeholder.png){#fig-q2-processing-challenges}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will identify the most selected processing challenges and discuss the related noisy-audio quality item from Section B.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support preprocessing, validation, noise handling, and separation requirements for the proposed prototype.

### Question 3: Usefulness of a Heart-Lung Sound Separation Prototype

This question evaluates whether respondents believe a simple prototype for heart-lung sound separation would be useful for students, researchers, or users working with biomedical audio. It helps determine whether the proposed application has practical relevance.

![Usefulness of the proposed heart-lung sound separation prototype](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q3_prototype_usefulness_placeholder.png){#fig-q3-prototype-usefulness}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will explain whether respondent feedback supports the development of the proposed prototype.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support the overall system relevance and justify the application-based prototype scope.

### Question 4: Preferred System Features

This question collects user preferences on the most important system features, such as uploading mixed cardiopulmonary audio, preprocessing noisy audio, separating heart and lung sounds, previewing separated audio, downloading outputs, viewing history, and viewing evaluation results.

![Preferred system features](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q4_preferred_features_placeholder.png){#fig-q4-preferred-features}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will summarize the most preferred features and may mention processing history preferences from Section C.

**Requirement implication:** The result will help prioritize the functional requirements of the prototype.

### Question 5: Preferred Output After Separation

This question identifies the preferred output after sound separation, such as audio files only, waveform visualization, spectrogram visualization, evaluation metrics, or a combination of these outputs. The related result-display question from Section D will be discussed in text only.

![Preferred output after sound separation](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q5_output_after_separation_placeholder.png){#fig-q5-output-after-separation}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will describe the preferred result format and explain how it affects output presentation.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support output design requirements, including whether the prototype should show audio files, waveform displays, spectrogram displays, or evaluation information.

### Question 6: Importance of Audio Preview Function

This question measures how important respondents consider previewing separated heart and lung sounds before downloading them. The related download-importance question from Section C will be mentioned in the discussion only.

![Importance of previewing separated heart and lung sounds](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q6_preview_importance_placeholder.png){#fig-q6-preview-importance}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will explain whether respondents consider previewing separated outputs to be a core feature.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support preview and download requirements for separated heart and lung sound outputs.

### Question 7: Preferred Interface Style

This question identifies whether respondents prefer a simple interface, a detailed technical interface, or a balanced interface with a simple view and optional advanced details. Related ease-of-use and error-message questions from Section D will be discussed in text only.

![Preferred interface style](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q7_interface_style_placeholder.png){#fig-q7-interface-style}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will summarize the preferred interface style and discuss whether users need simple feedback and helpful error messages.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support usability requirements for an interface that is understandable to users with different technical backgrounds.

### Question 8: First Information Shown After Separation

This question asks what information respondents prefer to see first after separation is completed. Possible priorities include download buttons, audio preview players, waveform or spectrogram visualization, evaluation metrics, and processing status summary.

![Preferred first information after separation is completed](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q8_first_information_placeholder.png){#fig-q8-first-information}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will discuss the preferred first result information and may mention processing information and history preferences from Section C.

**Requirement implication:** The result will guide the result page design, including which output or status information should be emphasized first.

### Question 9: Importance of Evaluation Metrics

This question measures how important respondents consider evaluation metrics for the separated output. The related question about useful evaluation information from Section E will be discussed in text only.

![Importance of evaluation metrics for separated output](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q9_evaluation_metrics_placeholder.png){#fig-q9-evaluation-metrics}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will explain whether respondents expect the prototype to show evaluation information.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support evaluation requirements, such as displaying signal quality, separation quality, noise reduction information, or processing time when valid data is available.

### Question 10: Willingness to Use the Prototype

This question assesses whether respondents would use a prototype that separates mixed cardiopulmonary audio into heart and lung sound outputs. The open-ended improvement question from Section E will be discussed in text only after responses are collected.

![Willingness to use the cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype](figures/questionnaire/placeholders/q10_willingness_to_use_placeholder.png){#fig-q10-willingness-to-use}

**Finding:** Pending. This finding will be completed after Google Form responses are collected. The analysis will summarize user acceptance and identify improvement suggestions from written feedback.

**Requirement implication:** The result will support user acceptance, prototype refinement, and future improvement planning.

## Functional Requirements

Table @tbl-functional-requirements lists the preliminary functional requirements for the proposed prototype.

| Req ID | Requirement | Description |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Upload Audio File | The system shall allow the user to upload a mixed cardiopulmonary audio file for processing. |
| F2 | Validate Audio Format | The system shall validate the uploaded file type, file size, and basic audio readability before processing starts. |
| F3 | Preprocess Audio | The system shall apply suitable preprocessing steps such as resampling, normalization, segmentation, or noise reduction according to the selected workflow. |
| F4 | Run Cardiopulmonary Sound Separation | The system shall execute the selected machine learning-based separation pipeline on the validated and preprocessed recording. |
| F5 | Generate Heart Sound Output | The system shall produce a separated heart sound output from the mixed cardiopulmonary input. |
| F6 | Generate Lung Sound Output | The system shall produce a separated lung sound output from the mixed cardiopulmonary input. |
| F7 | Preview Separated Outputs | The system shall allow users to preview the separated heart and lung outputs before downloading them. |
| F8 | Download Separated Outputs | The system shall allow users to download the separated heart and lung sound files. |
| F9 | Display Processing Status | The system shall show processing status information such as validation result, processing progress, completion state, or failure message. |
| F10 | Display Evaluation Metrics | The system shall display suitable evaluation metrics when reference signals or valid evaluation data are available. |
| F11 | View Processing History | The system shall provide a processing history showing previous uploads and separation results when storage support is enabled. |

: Functional requirements for the cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype {#tbl-functional-requirements}

## Non-Functional Requirements

Table @tbl-nonfunctional-requirements lists the preliminary non-functional requirements for the proposed prototype.

| Req ID | Category | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| NF1 | Usability | The interface shall be understandable for users with different levels of technical experience. |
| NF2 | Performance | The system shall process reasonable audio file sizes within an acceptable time for prototype demonstration and evaluation. |
| NF3 | Reliability | The system shall handle invalid files, failed preprocessing, failed separation, and missing outputs with clear feedback. |
| NF4 | Maintainability | The system shall separate interface, validation, preprocessing, model, storage, and result management logic to support future updates. |
| NF5 | Security and Privacy | The system shall handle uploaded audio files carefully and avoid exposing or retaining files unnecessarily. |
| NF6 | Compatibility | The system shall support common audio formats where feasible and document any input limitations. |
| NF7 | Data Integrity | The system shall avoid overwriting outputs incorrectly and shall preserve the association between uploaded files, processing status, and generated outputs. |
| NF8 | Scalability | The system design shall allow future expansion, such as additional models, output visualizations, or evaluation metrics, without major restructuring. |

: Non-functional requirements for the cardiopulmonary sound separation prototype {#tbl-nonfunctional-requirements}

## User Requirements

Table @tbl-user-requirements summarizes the preliminary user requirements for the proposed prototype.

| User Requirement ID | User Need | Description |
|---|---|---|
| UR1 | Easy audio upload | The user needs to upload mixed cardiopulmonary audio easily through a clear interface. |
| UR2 | File validity feedback | The user needs to understand whether the uploaded file is valid before processing begins. |
| UR3 | Separated heart and lung outputs | The user needs separated heart and lung sound outputs after the separation process is completed. |
| UR4 | Output preview | The user needs to preview separated outputs before downloading them. |
| UR5 | Simple visual feedback | The user needs simple visual feedback such as waveform or spectrogram displays when these are supported by the prototype. |
| UR6 | Clear status and errors | The user needs clear processing status and error messages when validation or separation fails. |
| UR7 | Downloadable results | The user needs to download separated output files for review, reporting, or further analysis. |
| UR8 | Basic metrics or processing information | The user needs basic metrics or processing information when evaluation support is included. |

: User requirements for the proposed prototype {#tbl-user-requirements}

## Summary

This chapter presented the requirements analysis for the proposed system. The questionnaire is a required fact-finding method and has been designed to collect practical user feedback through Google Forms. Section A is summarized as respondent profile information, while Sections B to E are represented through 10 main requirement-focused analysis items. Since responses have not yet been collected, the findings and chart figures are left as placeholders to be completed after data collection. Preliminary functional, non-functional, and user requirements were defined based on the project scope, literature review, supervisor consultation, and planned questionnaire analysis.
